messages:
lena: FYI support escalation from Customer Zeta — they see a sudden p95 jump for text-generation API calls from APAC clients starting ~2026-03-15T15:10 IST. They report long TLS handshake times (~200-800ms) and overall request RTT +500-800ms. Attaching their curl timings and a couple of samples from their region. Can SRE/ingress triage? :eyes:

kai: on it. Which POP are their requests landing at? Any common client IP prefix or carrier?

lena: they gave two example client IPs (private in ticket, I pasted last octet): 203.116.58.x and 103.8.200.y. Their DNS resolves to api.redwood.ai (CNAME to our apac-anycast). I asked for exact region, they say Singapore mobile users mostly, but also some from Mumbai.

ingress-bot: [alert] apac-edge: TLS handshake p95 spike detected for service=api (15:08–15:12). Spike correlated with increased SYN retransmits. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/ALERT-1234

om: I pushed a quick synthetic from our singapore POP. Reproducing a p95 TLS time ~420ms. Running traceroute to customer IP shows an odd hairpin: packets leave sg-pop -> tokyo-pop -> back -> sg-pop. Posting traceroute and curl timings.

om: ```
# curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer} total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.ai/health
time_connect:0.025 time_appconnect:0.433 time_starttransfer:0.435 total:0.438
```

om: ```
# traceroute -n -w 1 -q 1 203.116.58.7
 1  10.10.20.1  0.8 ms
 2  100.64.1.12  1.2 ms
 3  203.119.5.6  2.3 ms  (sg-pop)
 4  54.248.12.9  180.4 ms (tokyo-pop)
 5  203.119.5.6  181.1 ms (back to sg-pop)
 6  203.116.58.7  181.8 ms
```

mira: that looks like asymmetric routing / anycast fallback — packets are being handed off to tokyo and then back to sg, causing extra RTT and handshake delay. Could be upstream transit or our route reflector/PE mis-advertising. Any recent BGP pushes or edge infra changes?

ryan: I don't see any deployment touching sg-pop routing configs. We did rotate a transit peer in apac yesterday at 03:00 UTC for routine maintenance — could be the cause. I'll pull BGP dumps and look at local RIBs.

carla: Customer Zeta is getting escalated to SEs, they're annoyed. Can we give a mitigation path so they can avoid impact? They asked if pinning to another region is possible temporarily.

kai: Short term mitigation options: 1) steer this customer's prefix to nearest healthy POP via steering policy (fast, but needs DNS TTL and client cache); 2) for hosted customers we can set a routing override in the edge control plane to prefer tokyo or mumbai POPs for their API key; 3) flip traffic to Dedicated fallback (if they have dedicated) — but Zeta is on hosted.

om: DNS steering requires low TTL; their TTL is 60s so it should be quickish. I can push a steering change to prefer ap-northeast-1 (tokyo) for that CIDR, but that risks sending them to tokyo only — might be worse for some Mumbai clients. Alternative: increase sg-pop weight for that AS path on our load balancer.

lena: customer asked for an ETA. Can we do a temporary routing override and monitor? Also they provided a client-side traceroute showing similar hairpin.

deploy-bot: Routing override request submitted: change_id=ROUTE-9876 by @om — target_weights: sg-pop:+20%, tokyo-pop:-20% — pending canary rollout.

om: starting canary rollout 15:28 UTC -> canary to 3% of apac requests. Monitoring p95 and TLS handshake times.

ingress-bot: Canary rollout deployed (change_id=ROUTE-9876). Metrics link: https://console.redwood/metrics/ROUTE-9876

om: initial canary looks promising — synthetic from singapore shows appconnect down from ~430ms to ~90ms. P95 for TLS in apac dropping from 420ms->95ms on canary traffic.

mira: good. Meanwhile I'm pulling RIBs and peering logs. If upstream transit is flapping, we'll need to coordinate with peering ops.

ryan: confirmed — at 14:55 UTC our route server started seeing a change in next-hop selection for a subset of client prefixes, likely from peer AS64512. I'm opening a ticket with transit provider: TP-4521.

lena: passing mitigation to customer: "We've deployed a temporary routing override that should reduce TLS handshake times for affected users within a few minutes. We're investigating root cause with our transit provider and will update." They responded :thumbsup: and will monitor.

carla: customer reported immediate improvement for most users, but a few corporate VPN users still see occasional spikes. Could be VPN routing through different egress.

kai: action items: 1) om/mira follow transit ticket TP-4521 and collect BGP dumps + pcap at sg-pop for time window; 2) monitor p95/p99 for next 24h and keep steering override in place until stable; 3) create postmortem if recurrence. I'll own 2.

om: collecting pcaps now. For reproducibility: we have a small script to run from any POP to a test client IP — use `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/zeta.pcap host <client-ip> and port 443` and curl test above.

mira: posted BGP dump snippet: ```
# show ip bgp 203.116.58.0/24
Paths: (1 available, best #1)
  64512 3356 4637
  Not advertised to any peer
  203.119.5.6 from 10.1.2.3 (10.1.2.3)
    Origin IGP, localpref 100, valid, external
```

ryan: transit provider acknowledging TP-4521, investigating AS-path prepends from their side. They saw flapping on one of their route-reflectors.

om: pcap shows SYN -> SYN/ACK reaches our tokyo router first, then traffic gets proxied back to sg-pop. That explains the extra 180ms.

lena: customer confirmed overall error rate down and p95 improved. They asked for a timeline to permanent fix.

mira: tentative RCA: transit route reflector bug caused temporary AS path selection to prefer tokyo POP for some APAC client prefixes; this resulted in packets traversing tokyo then back to singapore (hairpin), increasing RTT and TLS handshake times. Fix: coordinate with transit provider to stop path prepends and add more-specific /24 announcements in region, and update our PE filters to prefer local next-hop for known retail ISPs.

kai: next steps: - keep steering override for 12–24h, then gradually remove if stable - require transit provider confirm and provide RCA - update runbook with traceroute/tcpdump reproducibility steps - postmortem write-up with timeline and mitigations assigned to ryan/mira/om

carla: I told the customer we'll send a summary and the postmortem link once ready. They appreciated the quick mitigation.

deploy-bot: Routing override rolled back at 16:40 UTC (change_id=ROUTE-9876) after metrics stable for 45m.

ingress-bot: apac-edge metrics: TLS handshake p95 returned to baseline (~90ms) and SYN retransmits normalized.

lena: closing the support escalation ticket and creating internal incident for RCA follow-up. Thanks everyone — great cross-team response. :clap:
